title: Dynamics of Moral Behavior in Heterogeneous Populations of Learning Agents
reasoning: The paper explores the dynamics of moral decision-making within populations of artificial agents using Reinforcement Learning (DQN). It explicitly benchmarks various moral reward functions based on philosophical frameworks such as utilitarianism, deontology, and virtue ethics, but it does so in a game-theoretic simulation (Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) rather than using Large Language Models or NLP systems.
